item.title: People urged not to assume all information has been given in Michael Gaine investigation as fresh appeal issued
item.description: People are being urged not to assume that someone else has already provided all the information as the Michael Gaine investigation continues. Regional Chief Superintendent for the Southern Garda Region, Colm O’Sullivan has issued a fresh appeal to the public for information. 56-year-old Mike Gaine was reported missing from his home outside Kenmare on March 20th; the case was upgraded to a homicide investigation in late April. item.title: Company behind major plans for Phoenix Cinema in Dingle intend to apply for planning permission
item.description: The company behind major plans for the historic Phoenix Cinema in Dingle has announced its intention to apply for planning permission. The cinema was bought in late 2024 by visual artist Yvonne McGuinness and her husband, Oscar-winning actor Cillian Murphy. Since then, several public meetings have been held, allowing the community to have a say in the future of the not-for-profit regional cultural centre planned for the site. item.title: Kerry County Council to salt roads tonight as frosty conditions expected
item.description: Kerry County Council will be salting roads tonight, as frosty conditions are expected. Temperatures are forecast to fall below zero overnight bringing freezing conditions. The council says it will spread salt on the county's main roads from 10.30pm to ensure safer travelling conditions on Christmas Day. Advertisement Kerry County Council is urging people to reduce their speed over the coming days and to stay safe over Christmas.

item.title: Christmas day swims in Kerry tomorrow
item.description: Christmas swims are taking place across Kerry tomorrow. Local charities are set to benefit from funds raised by all the swims. They’re starting in Portmagee at half past 10 in support of Dromid Cancer Care Support Car. Advertisement The Kenmare swims begins at 11am to in aid of the Kerry Mental Health Association At the same time Killarney swimmers will raise funds at Muckross Lake in aid of mental health charity Aware. item.title: Christian leaders in Kerry issue Christmas Day messages
item.description: Christian leaders in Kerry have issued their Christmas Day messages. The Roman Catholic bishop of the Diocese of Kerry, Ray Browne reminded people that love, faith and hope lie at the heart of the season. He encouraged those who are experiencing difficulty to take comfort in the simplicity of the first Christmas, when Mary and Joseph showed that fulfilment does not depend on everything being ideal. item.title: North Kerry CAMHS look back review still not published
item.description: There is still no indication as to when the review of cases of children and teenagers who attended North Kerry CAMHS will be published. The look back review involving around 300 files was announced three years ago but still has not been finalised by the HSE. Campaigner Davin Godfrey is a former service user of child and adolescent mental health services in North Kerry. item.title: Kerry’s Live Register dropped by 2% in year
item.description: Kerry’s Live Register fell by over 2% in 12 months. In November this year, over 5,800 (5,848) people in Kerry signed on the Live Register. That’s down from more than 5,900 (5,978) during November last year (2024). Advertisement The CSO has released figures for the numbers signing on the live register for the first 11 months of the year.
